native_mcp_support.notes: No native MCP at model level. MCP can be wired in via serving stacks (vLLM, SGLang) that expose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, but the model itself has no native MCP protocol. Phi-4-mini and multimodal document function-calling via a custom chat template; Phi-4 base does not document function-calling.

skills_concept.notes: No formal skills/extensions concept for self-hosted Phi models. Azure AI Foundry hosting may expose agent-level features, but these are platform-layer, not model-native.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Model card states 'cutoff date of June 2024 and earlier for publicly available data'

context_window_tokens.notes: config.json: max_position_embeddings=16384, original_max_position_embeddings=16384, rope_scaling=null. Azure Foundry also lists input+output as 16,384 tokens each.

input_output_shared.notes: Azure Foundry shows input 16,384 and output 16,384; total pool is 16,384 shared (input+output must fit within 16K). Self-hosted: serving stack enforces this.

max_input_tokens.notes: Azure Foundry documents 16,384 input tokens. Self-hosted: max_position_embeddings=16384 sets the hard ceiling.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: No documented default. Self-hosted via vLLM/Ollama, max_new_tokens is set per-request; no vendor-published default for open-weight deployment.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: Azure Foundry documents output up to 16,384 tokens. Self-hosted: ceiling is the 16K context window.

extended_context.notes: No extended/beta context documented. rope_scaling is null in config.json. Native ceiling is 16K.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Phi-4 is not a reasoning model (no chain-of-thought token budget). Phi-4-reasoning is a separate model. N/A here.

tokenizer_family.notes: tokenizer_config.json lists tokenizer_class=GPT2Tokenizer with vocabulary tokens matching tiktoken o200k_base at indices 0-100255, plus Microsoft-added special tokens (100256-100351). config.json vocab_size=100352. The base 100K tokens are identical to tiktoken o200k_base; Microsoft extended with 96 special-purpose tokens.

image_token_rule.notes: Phi-4 is text-only; no image token rule.

audio_token_rule.notes: Phi-4 is text-only; no audio token rule.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Approximate for English text with tiktoken-compatible tokenizer. Use HF AutoTokenizer for exact counts.

function_calling.notes: Azure Foundry explicitly lists 'Tool calling: No' for Phi-4. The HF model card does not document a function-calling chat template or format (unlike Phi-4-mini which has <|tool|> tokens). Phi-4 base was released Dec 2024 without function-calling instruction tuning.

native_mcp.notes: No native MCP support at model level. Requires serving-stack wrappers.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Not documented; function calling not natively supported in Phi-4.

max_tools_hard.notes: No documented hard limit. Phi-4 does not natively support function calling, so tools are limited by context window (16K) if injected as text.

max_tools_practical.notes: CRITICAL: 16K total window is severely constraining for MCP tool definitions. A single MCP server's tool definitions commonly consume 2-8K tokens. With only 16K total, even 3-5 verbose tool definitions can consume 30-50% of the window, leaving little room for conversation history and output. This is the smallest window in the open-weight roster — MCP footprint risk is highest here.

tool_definition_shape.notes: When function calling is approximated via prompt injection with vLLM/OpenAI-compatible serving, tools are submitted in OpenAI function-call JSON format. No native tool format documented in model card.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool definitions serialized into the prompt count as input tokens. At 16K window this is critical — even modest tool footprints consume a large fraction.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No deferred/lazy tool loading at model level. No equivalent of Claude Code's defer_loading.

max_tool_name_len.notes: Not documented; depends on serving stack.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Phi-4 has no documented schema-size limits beyond the 16K context window ceiling. All tool definitions must fit within this shared pool. In practice this means MCP deployments must be tightly scoped — a single large MCP server (50+ tools at ~200 tok/def = 10K+) would consume the majority of the context before any user message.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No vendor cap; description counts against context window.

max_request_size.notes: No vendor byte cap; bounded by serving config (vLLM --max-model-len / --max-num-batched-tokens) and GPU memory.

max_tool_result_size.notes: Context-bound; tool results count against max_model_len.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Depends on the model chat-template tool-call parser; see parallel_tool_calls.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: Set by the agent host/framework, not the model.

max_total_tools.notes: No vendor cap. Effective ceiling ≈ (context_window − output headroom) ÷ avg tool-definition tokens, set by serving config. Client hosts may cap lower (Cursor ~40, Claude Desktop ~100).

tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Open-weight: the model API layer imposes NO tool count/size caps. Binding limits come from (1) the serving stack — vLLM/SGLang max_model_len, max_num_batched_tokens, GPU KV-cache; (2) the model chat-template tool-call parser (must match --tool-call-parser); (3) the agent host (Cursor ~40-tool cap, Claude Desktop ~100). vLLM's default context is often 16K which silently truncates tool calls — raise --max-model-len.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop/5-depth/no-oneOf. (Gemini/Anthropic have their own, looser keyword rules — captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.)

skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: No documented fixed system-prompt overhead. The chat template (tokenizer_config.json) adds minimal special tokens per turn (<|im_start|>, <|im_sep|>, <|im_end|>). System prompt counts as input tokens against the shared 16K pool.

prompt_caching.notes: No vendor-level prompt caching for open-weight self-hosted deployment. Some serving frameworks (vLLM with --enable-prefix-caching, SGLang with RadixAttention) support KV-cache prefix reuse, but this is operator-configured, not model-native.

memory_feature.notes: No persistent memory feature at model level.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Open weights — self-hosted compute cost only. Azure AI Foundry serverless pricing page shows '$-' (currently free at serverless tier as of 2026-06-21 per https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/ai-foundry-models/microsoft/). Self-host = operator pays GPU/cloud costs.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Same as input: self-hosted compute only.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: N/A for self-hosted; prefix caching via vLLM/SGLang reduces GPU compute but has no per-token billing.

billing_unit.notes: Self-hosted compute (GPU hours / cloud instance cost).

license.notes: Model card and LICENSE file on HF confirm MIT license.

max_context_documented.notes: No documented extended context beyond 16K for Phi-4. The rope_theta=250000 was tuned for 16K; no longer RoPE scaling config documented.

self_host.framework_tool_calling_notes: Phi-4 does not have native function-calling post-training. When served via vLLM/SGLang with an OpenAI-compatible API, tools can be submitted in OpenAI function-call JSON format, but the model was not specifically trained to follow this format reliably. Phi-4-mini is the recommended choice for function calling within the Phi-4 family.

models.notes: Phi-4 (14B, Dec 2024) is the largest and most capable base text model in the Phi-4 family. Its 16K context window is the smallest in this open-weight comparison, making it the highest-risk model for MCP deployments with large tool footprints. A single MCP server with 30+ tools easily consumes 50-100% of the available context, leaving no room for conversation history. Function calling is not officially supported (Azure Foundry: Tool calling No). Best suited for latency-sensitive text/reasoning tasks with minimal tool use.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Model card: 'This is a static model trained on offline datasets with the cutoff date of June 2024 for publicly available data.' Trained November–December 2024.

The base vocab is o200k_base (200K tokens) extended with Phi-4-mini special tokens including <|tool|>, <|/tool|>, <|tool_call|>, <|/tool_call|>, <|tool_response|>.

function_calling.notes: Model card explicitly documents a 'Tool-enabled function-calling format' with <|tool|>...<|/tool|> system-prompt wrapper for JSON tool definitions, and <|tool_call|>...<|/tool_call|> for model responses. Function calling is a primary use case listed in intended uses.

native_mcp.notes: No native MCP protocol. Uses a custom JSON-in-system-prompt format for tools. Azure Foundry lists 'Tool calling: No' for the hosted endpoint, though the model weights support it via the custom format.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Not explicitly documented in model card. The custom tool format allows multiple tools in the system prompt, but whether multiple simultaneous calls per turn is trained is undocumented.

max_tools_hard.notes: No documented API-enforced hard limit on tool count. Practical ceiling is the 128K context window.

max_tools_practical.notes: Estimated from general small-model degradation patterns (Berkeley FCL: accuracy drops steeply past 30-50 tools for larger models; smaller 3.8B models tend to degrade earlier). 128K window gives more headroom than Phi-4's 16K, but the 3.8B parameter count limits reliable tool selection across large sets. Tier-4 estimate only.

tool_definition_shape.notes: Phi-4-mini uses a custom format: tools provided as a JSON array in the system prompt, wrapped by special tokens <|tool|>[{...}]<|/tool|>. Each tool definition is a JSON object with name, description, and parameters fields — structurally similar to OpenAI function format but injected via system prompt rather than as a separate API parameter. vLLM with OpenAI-compatible API may also accept openai_function format and translate internally.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool JSON serialized in the system prompt counts as input tokens. 128K window provides significantly more headroom than Phi-4, but the 3.8B parameter size means accuracy may degrade before the context window is saturated.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No deferred/lazy tool loading at model level.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Tools are injected as JSON in the system prompt between <|tool|> and <|/tool|> special tokens. Each tool JSON object is counted as input tokens. With 128K context, MCP tool footprint is less critical than Phi-4, but model capability at 3.8B may limit reliable selection from large tool sets. Red-team testing noted that 'the model could sometimes hallucinate function names or URLs' in function calling scenarios.

self_host.framework_tool_calling_notes: Phi-4-mini-instruct has native function-calling support via its custom <|tool|>/<|/tool|> chat template. When served via vLLM or SGLang with OpenAI-compatible API, tools can be submitted in the OpenAI function-call format and the framework translates to the model's native format. PhiCookBook (GitHub) provides function calling examples. Note: model card red-team testing found hallucination of function names/URLs in some function-calling scenarios.

models.notes: Phi-4-mini-instruct (3.8B, Feb 2025) is the recommended Phi-4 model for function-calling/MCP use cases — it explicitly documents tool/function calling with a dedicated format and has a 128K context window vs Phi-4's 16K. However, its 3.8B parameter count means reliable tool selection degrades faster than larger models. Excellent for edge/device deployment where function calling is needed with minimal GPU memory (fits in ~8GB VRAM with quantization).

image_token_rule.value: Dynamic high-definition (HD) transform via avg_pool_2d compression; up to 3,600 visual tokens per image depending on resolution
image_token_rule.notes: config.json embd_layer.image_embd_layer: use_hd_transform=true, crop_size=448, image_token_compression_cls=avg_pool_2d, hd_transform_order=sub_glb, with_learnable_separator=true. Phi-4-reasoning-vision (related model) documents up to 3,600 visual tokens for high-resolution inputs. Exact token count per image varies by resolution; no fixed per-image token rule documented.

audio_token_rule.value: Cascades encoder with time_reduction=8; audio processed at 80-dim mel features → ~1 token per 80ms of audio
audio_token_rule.notes: config.json audio_processor.config: time_reduction=8, input_size=80 (mel features), num_blocks=24. time_reduction=8 means 8 frames are compressed to 1 token. At 16kHz with standard 10ms frame shift, roughly ~12-13 tokens per second of audio. No precise per-second published in model card.

Key consideration: multimodal inputs (images/audio) compete with tool definitions for the 128K context budget. A high-resolution image can consume hundreds to thousands of tokens, directly reducing the number of MCP tools that can be loaded. MCP use should be evaluated per-session with actual image/audio token budgets in mind.

models.notes: Phi-4-multimodal-instruct (5.6B, Feb 2025) is the first open small model combining text, vision, and audio in a unified architecture. It shares the 128K context window and function-calling format with Phi-4-mini. Key MCP consideration: image and audio tokens consume the same shared pool as tool definitions — a single high-res image can consume thousands of tokens, directly reducing available tool budget. Ranked #1 on HuggingFace OpenASR leaderboard (WER 6.14%) at release. Requires trust_remote_code=True for all serving.
